classification.difficultyReason: Construct a two-stage suit array and count outcomes satisfying four different event conditions.

content.prompt: The four Aces and the four Kings are removed from a pack of playing cards. One card is taken from the set of four Aces and one card is taken from the set of four Kings. Construct an array for the outcomes of this experiment, and use it to find the probability that the two cards chosen:

inlines.text: S = Spades, H = Hearts, D = Diamonds, C = Clubs. Each pair is (Ace suit, King suit).
Use one row for each Ace and one column for each King. S = Spades, H = Hearts, D = Diamonds, C = Clubs. Entries are (Ace suit, King suit).

answer.worked:
Spades and Clubs are black. The favourable array entries are (S, S), (S, C), (C, S) and (C, C).
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{both black})&=\frac4{16}\\P(\text{both black})&=\frac14\end{align*}$$

Only (S, S) is favourable, out of 16 equally likely entries.
$$P(\text{both Spades})=\frac1{16}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: include at least one black card

answer.worked:
The S and C rows contain 8 favourable entries. In the H and D rows, the S and C columns give another 4. There are 12 favourable entries altogether.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{at least one black card})&=\frac{12}{16}\\P(\text{at least one black card})&=\frac34\end{align*}$$

The four diagonal entries (S, S), (H, H), (D, D) and (C, C) are favourable.
$$\begin{align*}P(\text{same suit})&=\frac4{16}\\P(\text{same suit})&=\frac14\end{align*}$$
